findings.breaking_input: On Windows set Path to `C:\Program Files\MyToolGit\cmd;C:\Windows\system32` and have `C:\Program Files\MyToolGit\bin\bash.exe` be a non-Git bash (for example a copy of WSL's launcher or a stub without /usr/bin). gitBashEnv's regex `^(.*[\\/]Git)[\\/]...` matches `MyToolGit` as a Git root, prepends its bin, and suppresses the WARN; the door's `bash arc-event.sh` then cannot write run.completed, so every answer still fails.
findings.why: The regex's `.*[\\/]Git` accepts any last path segment ending in `Git`, not only the exact `Git` directory, so a look-alike directory is trusted as Git for Windows.
findings.fix: Anchor the match to a path segment exactly `Git` (case-insensitive) separated on both sides, e.g. `/^(.*[\\/])Git[\\/](?:cmd|bin|usr[\\/]bin|mingw64[\\/]bin)[\\/]?$/i`, or verify `win32.basename(root).toLowerCase() === 'git'`.
findings.twin_of: A `grep 'face/src'` matched `arcface/src` inside a reference path -> a path grep is bounded on the left.

findings.breaking_input: On Windows, with the current directory on C: and the repo on D:, set Path to `\Program Files\Git\cmd;C:\Windows\system32` (a drive-relative PATH entry) and have Git installed at `C:\Program Files\Git`. gitBashEnv checks `\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` from C: and returns bashDir = `\Program Files\Git\bin`; the door child is spawned with cwd D:\repo, so that same PATH entry resolves to `D:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`, which does not exist, and the receipt still fails.
findings.why: The existence check resolves the relative root against the parent's cwd, while the PATH entry is later resolved by the child against the child's cwd; the two resolvers disagree.
findings.fix: Convert each root to an absolute path with `win32.resolve(root)` before the existence check and put the absolute path in the child's PATH, or refuse roots that are not absolute (drive letter or UNC).
findings.twin_of: A caller path opened on existsSync alone -> A path from a caller is a claim about a file; resolve it before trusting it.

findings.breaking_input: Start arc-face from a shell with `GIT_DIR=C:\other\.git` and `GIT_WORK_TREE=C:\other` exported. The spawn env is `{ ...bash.env, ARC_DASH_TOKEN: token }`, so the door child inherits those git location variables and its git reads/writes (spine, receipts) target `C:\other` instead of the repo the launcher resolved, so run.completed lands in the wrong repository and answers are not served.
findings.why: The launcher passes the whole parent environment to the door; git's location variables override the child's notion of which repository it is in.
findings.fix: Build the child env from `bash.env` minus `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR` and set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.
findings.twin_of: The resolver was fed another repo -> a child the door runs inherits the door's env minus git's location variables (`childEnv`).

findings.breaking_input: On Windows with no Git for Windows installed and `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` (WSL) first on PATH, run `node .claude/scripts/hq/arc-face.mjs`. gitBashEnv returns bashDir:null; the code writes a WARN and still spawns the door with the broken env, so the original MODEL_FAILED-on-every-answer failure continues.
findings.why: The launcher knows the door cannot write receipts in this configuration but only warns and proceeds; a known-broken run is not refused.
findings.fix: Exit non-zero with a named error when `process.platform === 'win32' && !bash.bashDir`, or probe `bash -c 'true'` with the constructed env and refuse if the probe fails.

findings.breaking_input: On Windows, create a directory at `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` (or `C:\evil\Git\bin\bash.exe` with a PATH entry `C:\evil\Git\cmd`) and run arc-face. existsSync returns true for the directory, so gitBashEnv reports a bashDir and suppresses the WARN; the later spawn of `bash` fails because it is a directory, and the receipt is not written.
findings.why: The check is existence, not a regular file; a directory named bash.exe is accepted as proof that Git bash is present.
findings.fix: Use `statSync` and require `isFile()` (and ideally execute a probe) before accepting a root.
findings.twin_of: `existsSync` accepted a directory as an executable, and a spawn error was an unhandled `'error'` event -> require `isFile()`, and every spawned child gets an `'error'` listener before anything else.

findings.breaking_input: Make a provider (or any child) write to stderr: `provider error: the gateway could not emit run.completed because the model timed out`. providerFault returns the receipt/WSL message, hiding the real timeout/provider fault; conversely a 429 with that phrase is no longer reported as busy.
findings.why: The receipt regex is not anchored to arc-run's own line, so any substring match wins over the more specific status-code and timeout branches.
findings.fix: Anchor the receipt test to the arc-run prefix (e.g. `/arc-run: could not emit run\.completed/`) and let other phrases fall through to their named causes.
